**Children’s Engagement With Digital Devices, Screen Time**  
(URL: [https://www.pewresearch.org/internet/2020/07/28/childrens-engagement-with-digital-devices-screen-time/](https://www.pewresearch.org/internet/2020/07/28/childrens-engagement-with-digital-devices-screen-time/))

*(Published July 2020\)*

* **More than one-third of parents w/ a child under 12 say their child began interacting w/ a smartphone before the age of 5**  
* Portion of parents say their child younger than 12 uses social media; use varies by age of child, parents’ level of education  
    * Relatively few parents of a child age 11 or younger say that, as far as they know, their child uses social media, though shares are higher for parents of children ages 9 to 11   
    * Despite most social media sites having age guidelines in place (usually restricting children under 13 from joining), some 13% of these parents say their child uses TikTok and 10% say their child uses Snapchat  
        * Just 5% say their child uses Instagram, and even fewer (3%) say their child uses Facebook  
        * Some 7% of parents say their child uses some other social media site  
    * Parents w/ a child age 9 to 11 are more likely than parents w/ child in younger age groups to say their child uses any of the social media platforms asked about in survey  
        * **E.g., 3 in 10 parents of a child age 9 to 11 say their child uses TikTok, compared with 11% of parents of a child between ages 5 and 8 and 3% of parents of children ages 4 and younger**  
        * **![][image1]**  
    * **Parents of a child age 11 or younger w/ a high school education or less are more likely than those w/ a postgraduate degree to say their child uses TikTok (19% vs. 6%)**  
        * Trend also holds for child’s use of Snapchat & Facebook  
* Parents are more likely to say their child under 12 uses a social media site if this child has their own smartphone  
    * **42% of parents who say their child has their own smartphone also say their child uses TikTok, and 31% say their child uses Snapchat**  
        * These shares fall to 10% or less across all platforms for parents who say their child does not have their own smartphone
